name: Yes Bank Ltd
title: Yes Bank Ltd - 532648 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Yes Bank exits FY26 at ~1% ROA with NIM 2.7% and GNPA 1.3%, but advances growth of 11% and a 14-15% FY27 target are the swing factors; RIDF rundown to ~INR 28,000 cr is a margin tailwind.

summary.headline: YES Bank Q4 FY26 net profit rose 44.7% YoY to INR 1,068 crore, with ROA of 1.0% and GNPA at a record-low 1.3%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered 44.7% YoY net profit growth to INR 1,068 crore and a 1.0% ROA, in line with guidance. NIM rose 10 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY to 2.7%, helped by RIDF and mandated-deposit rundown and CASA outperformance. Asset quality improved sharply, with GNPA at 1.3% and NNPA at 0.2%, while INR 341 crore of one-time standard-asset provisioning was taken in Q4. Advances grew 11.1% YoY to INR 2.73 lakh crore, with management signalling faster momentum and FY27 growth targeted at 13-15%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail disbursements grew ~41% YoY in Q4 FY26 and are above 20% YoY; Retail slippage in Q4 was INR 888 crore, lowest in 9 quarters. Retail book growth guided at 10-11% for FY27.

segments.name: Corporate and Commercial Banking
segments.commentary: Corporate book growing ~20% and Commercial Banking ~18%, per management. Commercial Banking is described as a preferred growth area.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Retail and branch-led deposits grew 13.5% YoY and form 58.4% of total deposits. CASA average-balance growth was 11.2% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth targeted at 13-15%, in line with or above industry; management said the book should grow in double digits.
RIDF and mandated deposits to fall from ~6% of total assets to below 5% by FY27. RIDF rundown in FY27 is at least INR 6,500 crore and could reach INR 9,000 crore from ~INR 28,000 crore at FY26 end.
Target ROA of 1% exit rate maintained; internal aim to add 25-50 bps of core ROA improvement over 2-3 years, excluding JC Flowers ARC write-backs.
Structural NIM target of 3.25-3.5% over 2-3 years; no near-term NIM guidance given.
SR recoveries of INR 800-1,000 crore expected in FY27; about INR 1,500 crore face value of SRs remains to be redeemed over the next few quarters.
Branch expansion of ~80 per year, about 400 over 4-5 years; 82 branches opened in FY26.
capex_capacity: 82 new branches opened in FY26, in line with guidance; plan of ~400 branches over 4-5 years (~80 per year).
Internal sourcing is ~50% of disbursals, of which ~60% comes through branches.
Management aims to invest across people, product, processes and technology; new rule engines and platform to support unsecured lending.
YES Grandeur, a premium banking suite for enterprises, was rolled out.
demand_pricing: Average deposit repricing front-loaded in April 2025; savings account rate cut by over 150 bps over the year to well below 4.5%, with another rate action in April 2026.
Yield on advances at March 2026 exit about 9.2%.
Management said it expects some mix compression as Retail grows slower than Corporate and Commercial, but mix to stabilise.
Management said MSME and larger clients are managing well with no signs of stress despite West Asia conflict; monitoring continues.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 15%+ next year, and how will CASA grow in line with loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 CA and SA each grew ~4% QoQ on average balances; CASA ~11% YoY on average. FY27 growth is guided at 13-15%, with sequential momentum accelerating from December to March.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mix shift between Retail, Wholesale and Commercial after the SMBC induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail disbursements are above 20% YoY and normalising at 20-25%; Retail book growth expected at 10-11% in FY27. Corporate is growing ~20%, and mix is expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: How did the bond yield spike affect treasury and AFS reserves?
qa_highlights.answer: The trading book is small. AFS reserve is about negative INR 100 crore at March 31, with a swing of ~INR 200 crore. Most of the SLR book sits in HTM, and CET-1 absorbed ~10 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 340 crore one-time standard-asset provision?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 341 crore of provisioning was taken in Q4 under evolving and prudent policies, not linked to any credit issue. It was funded by SR recoveries of ~INR 450 crore and a INR 288 crore write-back from one corporate account.

qa_highlights.question: What is the next ROA milestone, and how sustainable is 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank exited FY26 at 1% ROA. Internal aim is 25-50 bps core ROA improvement, with some JC Flowers ARC write-backs still to come in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What were credit card and personal loan slippages in INR crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit card slippage was about INR 133-140 crore and personal loan slippage about INR 160-180 crore; the figures were corrected during the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will branch expansion and branch share of disbursals change?
qa_highlights.answer: The plan is about 80 branches a year, aligned to deposit growth, credit growth and credit quality in each pin code. Branches supply ~60% of the ~50% of disbursals sourced internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff profile beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 and FY29 will see equal reductions, similar to FY27, with thinner runoff in FY29-FY30 as maturities taper.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AT1 case status?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter is sub judice, with Supreme Court hearings complete and judgment reserved. Management declined to comment on the likely outcome.

risks_watch: Pace of RIDF and mandated-deposit runoff, which drives the margin tailwind; FY27 runoff of INR 6,500-9,000 crore.
Whether Retail disbursement growth converts into book growth at 10-11%, and whether slippage stays near the Q4 lows.
Dependence on JC Flowers ARC write-backs (~INR 1,500 crore face value remaining) for part of ROA.
AT1 bond Supreme Court judgment, with a potential impact on the balance sheet; the outcome is unquantified.
Second-order effects of the West Asia conflict and rising G-sec yields on MSME credit and the HTM book.
summary.management_tone: Confident and measured on profitability and asset quality, with the new CEO signalling steady, calibrated growth. Management was cautious on near-term NIM and FY27 growth, declined to guide on NIM and AT1, and gave specific numbers where it had them.
key_quotes: In line with our guidance, Bank reported an ROA for the quarter of 1%.
the lowest ever that we have seen in the last 24 quarters and amongst the top quartile in our peer set
So, we will work hard and to make sure that we are driving each of these vectors to the right direction.

adds.what: ~80 new branches per year (82 opened in FY26), ~400 over 4-5 years

growth.why: FY27 advances growth guided at 13-15% (midpoint 14%), backed partly by ~80 branches a year and retail/corporate momentum, but no concrete loan-order or capacity numbers tie to the guide; Q4 PAT rose 44.7% YoY on NIM and lower provisions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM rose 10 bps QoQ to 2.7% in Q4 on RIDF and mandated-deposit rundown, with FY27 runoff of INR 6,500-9,000 crore, but management gave no near-term NIM guidance and a structural 3.25-3.5% target is 2-3 years out; offsets include Retail mix dilution and yield on advances at ~9.2%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management guides ~80 branches a year (82 opened in FY26) toward ~400 over 4-5 years, so new branches keep coming on stream each quarter, though the brief does not tie these to a volume number.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances guided to grow 13-15% in FY27 from 11.1% YoY at Q4 FY26 (INR 2.73 lakh crore), with Corporate growing ~20% and Retail disbursements above 20% YoY, though Retail book guided only 10-11%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Branch rollout is a standing plan of ~80 a year; no utilisation or capacity-constraint figure is given, and the brief cites no board-level capex plan beyond branches and technology spend.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 PAT rose 44.7% YoY to INR 1,068 crore with ROA at 1.0% exit and SR recoveries of ~INR 1,550 crore in FY26 against INR 1,200 crore guided, but FY27 guidance was just set as new, and the brief shows management cautious on NIM and growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include slower RIDF runoff, a Retail book at 10-11% growth versus >20% disbursements, reliance on ~INR 1,500 crore of remaining SR face value for ROA, and West Asia and G-sec yield pressure on MSME credit and the HTM book (CET-1 absorbed ~10 bps).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: YES Grandeur (premium enterprise suite) has just rolled out and new rule engines and platforms for unsecured lending are in build, but no launch dates or product counts are given.

rows.label: RIDF and mandated-deposit runoff
rows.why: RIDF and mandated deposits fall from ~6% of total assets to below 5% by FY27, with a runoff of at least INR 6,500 crore (up to INR 9,000 crore) from ~INR 28,000 crore at FY26 end, and FY28-FY29 runoff equal to FY27.

rows.label: AT1 bond Supreme Court judgment
rows.why: The matter is sub judice with hearings complete and judgment reserved; the outcome is unquantified and management declined to comment.

rows.label: Security Receipt recoveries feeding ROA
rows.why: SR recoveries of INR 800-1,000 crore are expected in FY27 with ~INR 1,500 crore face value still to redeem, and FY26 recoveries were ~INR 1,550 crore versus INR 1,200 crore guided.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, asset quality and the RIDF runoff, but cautious on near-term NIM and declined to guide on NIM or the AT1 case; analysts pushed on the growth ramp to 15%+, the INR 341 crore one-time standard-asset provision, and the sustainability of SR-driven ROA.
